sentences.text: After connectivity is restored, audit processing shall treat reconciled contingency actions as part of the same operational record as actions taken during Normal Operations.
The Regional Flow Platform shall record slot compliance events in the Audit Event Ledger using the operating date, flight identifier, airport, runway direction, and applicable regulation reference.

Each compliance assessment shall compare the Calculated Takeoff Time, the Target Off Block Time, actual off-block time, and actual takeoff time against the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
The Slot Compliance State shall indicate whether a flight was compliant, early, late, exempted, substituted, cancelled, or pending review at the end of the traffic period.
The Audit Event Ledger shall preserve the time source applied by the Time Synchronization Service so that later review can distinguish operational delay from data latency.
User decisions entered through the Airport CDM Portal shall be linked to the authenticated role provided by the Identity Access Service.
The Collaborative Decision Log shall retain the stated reason, decision time, affected flight, and visible operational context for each material change to a slot or sequence.
The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the permission email to justify an approved slot substitution during post-operations review.
Substitution records shall show the original flight, replacement flight, assigned Calculated Takeoff Time, acceptance status, and any subsequent cancellation or reversion.
When an Aircraft Operator Representative proposes a substitution, the audit trail shall capture whether the change preserved the constraints of the active Ground Delay Program.
The Slot Coordinator shall review substitution activity after operations to confirm that priority rules were applied consistently across participating operators.
Late operational changes shall be distinguished from planned updates by comparing the change timestamp with the freeze horizon held in the Business Rules Registry.
Changes made inside the freeze horizon shall require a reason code and shall be visible to the Regional Flow Manager during post-operations review.
The Tower Sequence Manager and Ramp Movement Board shall provide actual movement milestones that support independent verification of slot performance.
Surface movement evidence from the Surface Surveillance Adapter shall be retained long enough to support dispute resolution and regulatory audit requests.
Capacity changes made through the Capacity Assessment Module shall be correlated with the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate used at the time of allocation.
The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall aggregate compliance outcomes by carrier, route group, regulation, airport operating configuration, and time band.
Aggregated metrics shall support review of systemic lateness without exposing commercially sensitive detail beyond authorized roles.
The Data Governance Steward shall verify that audit fields required for slot performance reporting remain complete, immutable, and traceable to approved data definitions.
The System Support Engineer shall investigate technical gaps when audit sequences show missing events, duplicate updates, or inconsistent timestamps.

The Regional Flow Manager shall use the Post Operations Report to identify whether noncompliance resulted from operator choice, airport constraint, airspace constraint, weather impact, or system issue.
The Airport Duty Manager shall review late airport-driven changes that affected multiple flights and shall record whether the operational justification was valid.
Findings from the review shall feed adjustments to tolerance values, reason code definitions, and training material, subject to change control.
All audit outputs shall be retained according to the approved records schedule and shall remain searchable for compliance investigations, performance meetings, and lessons-learned activity.
